name: cloud_normalise
description: Turn identified cloud log exports into canonical rows, offline, and keep everything an adapter cannot read. Input: CSV, JSON (an array, one object, or an envelope such as entries, items or value), JSON Lines and gzip of those, one file, several (paths) or directories of them; the format is read from the content. Seven adapters read documented shapes (no real export exists; fixtures are authored from field lists, never copied from a vendor page): gcp_audit reads a Cloud Logging LogEntry whose protoPayload is a google.cloud.audit.AuditLog (principal and its delegation chain, service, method, resource, status, caller address and user agent, insertId, timestamp against receiveTimestamp, the log type from logName, the monitored resource); kubernetes_audit reads audit.k8s.io/v1 Event records, alone, as JSON Lines or in an EventList (audit id, stage, level, verb, request URI, user, groups, impersonation, source addresses, object reference, response status, both timestamps, annotations): a record is one stage and one row, so the stages of one audit id are separate rows and are never merged into one action; entra_directory_audit reads a Microsoft Graph directoryAudit (id, category, correlation id, result and reason, activity, logging service, operation type, the initiator as user or application kept apart from the target resources, and each target's modified properties, with change_topics, the words of the activity, category and operation names that point at consent, grant, revocation, delegation, a role or a credential, from this tool's own list and not a classification Microsoft documents); azure_activity_log reads an Azure Activity log record (JSON, as the REST list's value array, as an envelope or as lines, or a CSV whose header carries the same field names; eventTimestamp and submissionTimestamp, operationName, status and subStatus, caller, claims kept whole, authorization with action and scope, resourceId, correlationId, level, category, properties, httpRequest, eventDataId): a start and its completion are separate rows of one correlation id and are never merged, the scope and resource ids are printed as they are, the subscription is read from the resource id, and a status of Started or Accepted is an unknown outcome, never a success; workspace_activities reads Google Workspace Reports API activities (id with time, uniqueQualifier, applicationName and customerId, actor, ipAddress, events with type, name and parameters; JSON, as the response's items array, an envelope or lines): one row per event, the parameter bag kept whole (name, value, multiValue, boolValue and the other value members as written), parameters_by_name, before_after for parameters named old_X and new_X, topic_hints (the same kind of hint as change_topics), the actor as the principal and the targets only as parameters, an outcome of unknown because no result field is read, a value under a parameter named like a secret withheld in every value member, and the values of every parameter treated as sensitive; the Google documentation pages were NOT read, so the shape, the application, event and parameter names are NOT checked against a Google page, and the adapter takes every name from the record; aws_s3_access_log reads the S3 server access log, a space-separated text file with one request per line (the 27 fields the AWS page lists: bucket owner, bucket, bracketed time, remote IP, requester, request id, operation, key, request URI, HTTP status, error code, bytes sent, object size, total time, turn-around time, referer, user agent, version id, host id, signature version, cipher suite, authentication type, host header, TLS version, access point ARN, aclRequired, source region): - is null, fields the page does not list that follow the last one are counted (unknown_trailing_fields) and kept in the row and the raw line, a record with fewer fields keeps the ones it has and counts the missing, a quoted field that holds a quote of its own is counted, and a line that does not have the time field or does not quote the URI, referer and user agent where the format does is rejected; aws_vpc_flow reads VPC Flow Logs as delivered text: the field names come from the header line of the file (a later header line, as in files put end to end, replaces it), every field the AWS page lists for versions 2 to 11 is known (the page lists no field for version 6), a name it does not list is kept and counted, start and end are Unix seconds, a record with no header line is read only in the 14-field version 2 default order (or in the order vpc_flow_fields names) and any other is rejected, and a log-status of NODATA or SKIPDATA is a row of kind no_flow_record with no packet or byte count lifted, never a flow of zero traffic. Every row has: provider, adapter, tenant (a gcp project, organisation or folder; the Kubernetes and Entra records name none and the row says so), principal, action, resource, outcome (success, failure, or unknown when the record says nothing, with its basis), the raw time and the UTC time, a locator (file, record, line, offset in characters of the decoded text, which is the byte offset only for ASCII text), a duplicate annotation, the parser label and the whole record, cleaned. A time with no zone is never read as UTC: time_utc is null, time_status says no_zone and time_raw is kept; a day/month/year string is not guessed either. A record that parsed and that no adapter reads (for the requested provider), a malformed line, a truncated record and a record larger than max_record_bytes go to rejected.jsonl with the reason and the locator, and are counted in coverage as rejected, unsupported or malformed: none is dropped. A text file is recognised by its first line (a version number, a header line of flow log field names, or an S3 record), never by its name; format s3log or vpcflow names a text file the first line does not identify. Outputs, under out_dir (default: cloud-normalise under $OUT in a job, work/<agent>/cloud-normalise otherwise): normalised.jsonl (every row; the answer carries one page), rejected.jsonl and coverage.json (per source file: format, records read, rows, rejected, unsupported and malformed, the observed time range, pagination markers such as nextPageToken or @odata.nextLink, the first failures, and the status). A read that ended early or left anything out publishes normalised.partial.jsonl and coverage.partial.json; an output is never replaced by a smaller one, or by any other: a file already at an output name is kept (the new one is kept beside it as name.2.ext, or is the file when the bytes are equal). A duplicate (the same record id and stage seen again) is annotated and kept; nothing is deduplicated. Duplicates are annotated among the first 500000 distinct record keys, and the coverage says when the annotation stopped. `status` and `status_basis` say whether every record of the supplied files was read and turned into a row; complete says nothing about whether the export holds everything the provider logged (export completeness is not logging completeness). A file that names a next page (nextPageToken, @odata.nextLink) keeps the run partial. provider is auto (each record is given to the first adapter that recognises it) or one of gcp, kubernetes, entra, azure, workspace, aws_s3 and aws_vpc (a JSON or CSV record that is not that provider's is rejected, named; a text file of the other kind is not read and is listed as unsupported). principal is a regex (at most 200 characters, a pattern of a known exponential shape is refused, every test is timed at a quarter of a second) matched against the principal as it is printed, never against a withheld original. One clock: time_limit_seconds (default 420, at most 480, the call allows 600) covers the listing of directories, the reading, the withholding and the writing of the rows; a run that reaches it is partial and names the files it did not read. A termination signal ends the run with a partial coverage file (coverage.partial.json), one line of JSON on stdout and exit 128 plus the signal. Documentation: the S3 server access log fields and the VPC Flow Log fields per version were read from the AWS documentation pages named in tests/fixtures/cloud-normalise/SOURCES.json on 2026-11-04 (page URLs and what each supports are there). The Workspace Reports API shape and every Workspace name are the work card's and NOT checked against a Google page. All Azure and Workspace names and layouts here are unchecked against vendor documentation. The Azure Activity log field names are the work card's and were NOT checked against a vendor page (Azure documentation was not read): the layout of the nested objects (a value and a localizedValue), the words a status takes, and the column layout of the portal's own CSV export are not verified, and a CSV whose header does not carry the field names is rejected row by row and counted. The GCP, Kubernetes and Entra field lists were not read from vendor pages either. NOT measured: whether the provider logged everything, how long it kept it, whether the export holds all of what was logged, whether a principal was the person it names, or what a request did beyond what its record says. SENSITIVE: principal names, addresses and user agents are in the rows. Withholding is the shared block of every pack that withholds, with a 1 MiB gate here: identifiers (record, audit and correlation ids, project ids, object ids) are printed as they are; every other string goes through the credential rules only; a field named like a secret goes through the name layer. A Kubernetes request or response body that is a Secret object (an objectRef of secrets, or a body of kind Secret or SecretList) is replaced whole by a marker. The values of Entra modified properties are sensitive: a property whose name says password, secret, credential or token, or is named like a secret, has its old and new values withheld, and every other value goes through the credential rules. A field named or shaped like a credential is withheld and its original written only with write_values, in a job, to a mode 0600 file under $OUT: run as a job with secret_output: true when the case treats the export as sensitive. Known gaps: a secret with neither a credential name nor a token shape, and a Secret body that is neither under secrets nor of kind Secret, are printed; the Entra portal's own CSV layout is not read; a CSV is read only when its header carries the Graph property names or the Azure field names; the S3 CloudWatch JSON form of the access log is not read; a request URI, referer or user agent that holds a quote followed by a space and a status can move a field of an S3 line (the field count, the time field and the quoting of the three quoted fields are checked, and a line that fails them is rejected); a flow log whose delivered file has no header line and is not in the version 2 default order needs vpc_flow_fields; a text line longer than max_record_bytes stops that file, named; the Azure authorization object is kept in raw_record as authorization_object (the name layer withholds a field named authorization whole); nothing is read from archives (.zip, tar: named, not read).

path.description: One export file or a directory of them (the files of a directory are read in name order, then its subdirectories); from a directory only names ending .json, .jsonl, .ndjson, .csv, .log, .txt or .gz are read (name any other file, such as an S3 log object that has no extension, by its path)

paths.description: Several files or directories, read in the order given; a file listed twice is read once

provider.description: auto (default: each record goes to the first adapter that recognises it), gcp, kubernetes, entra, azure, workspace, aws_s3 or aws_vpc; a JSON or CSV record that is not the named provider's is rejected, named, and a text file of another kind (an S3 server access log or a VPC Flow Log) is not read and is listed as unsupported

format.description: auto (default: from the content), csv, json, jsonl, s3log or vpcflow (a text file); a file whose content contradicts it is not read and is listed as unsupported. s3log and vpcflow also name a text file whose first line does not identify it

delimiter.description: CSV delimiter, one character (default a comma)

vpc_flow_fields.description: VPC Flow Log field names in the order of the log's format, separated by spaces or commas, for a file that has no header line and is not in the 14-field version 2 default order (use it with format vpcflow when the first line does not identify the file); a header line in the file replaces it

out_dir.description: Directory for normalised.jsonl, rejected.jsonl and coverage.json, under the run directory (in a job, under $OUT: name it work/<your agent id>/..., which becomes $OUT). Default: cloud-normalise under $OUT in a job, work/<agent>/cloud-normalise otherwise. A file already at an output name is kept and the new one is named beside it

principal.description: Case-insensitive regex (at most 200 characters) over the principal as printed; only matching rows are written (the rest are counted in records_filtered_out); a pattern of a known exponential shape is refused, and every test is timed (a quarter of a second)

limit.description: Rows of each list returned inline (default 500, an inline page size); the whole is always in the files the answer names

max_expanded_bytes.description: Most bytes read from one file after decompression (default 4 GiB); a file that reaches it is partial and says so

max_record_bytes.description: Most text held while one record is read (default 16 MiB; a CSV line too); a larger record is rejected, located and listed, never cut (in an array or an envelope it is skipped by scanning to its end without holding it, and the records after it are read)

time_limit_seconds.description: Stop reading after this many seconds (default 420, at most 480, so the answer is written well inside the 600 seconds a call has); the limit is checked inside a record too; what was read is kept, the answer is partial and names the files not read

write_values.description: Write the originals of the values withheld from the answer to a mode 0600 file under $OUT. The manifest declares secret output for it: a job with write_values runs as secret output whether or not the agent set the flag, and its values file is sealed sensitive. Honoured only in a job whose SECRET_OUTPUT is 1; outside a job, or in a job that is not secret output, it is refused as JSON and nothing is written
